# Kelvin Okuda: tools

One line per tool. Machine-readable detail: products.json.

- Toilet Paper (App, Documents): Turns YAML and Markdown into BPMN, flowcharts, RACI matrices, icon pictures, Word documents and decks. No language model inside. toilet-paper/index.html
- Vault Index (MCP server, Knowledge): Hybrid search over a folder of Markdown notes, for people and for agents. No language model in the index, and nothing leaves the PC. vault-index/index.html
- Vault Sources (Agent, Knowledge): Brings videos and articles into your notes as sourced files, ranks what to watch against your own open questions, and proposes concept updates that only an explicit accept applies. vault-sources/index.html
- Capy (App, Knowledge): A desktop app that keeps Claude Code, Codex and Gemini sessions together, keeps API and plan accounts apart, checks every file write and shows what your key spends. capy/index.html
- AI Spend View (App, Operations): Shows each person their monthly spend on an AI gateway, from a daily capture. The numbers stay on your PC and in your profile folder. ai-spend-view/index.html
- Autodev (Agent, Building): An OpenCode model executes the task, Claude plans and reviews, and the tests are checked by mutation. Code waits for your ok. A team lead step caps how much work the free model gets. autodev/index.html
- Study Quest (App, Learning): Flashcards and battles over a study plan, with a save state. Study answers sync back to your notes vault. study-quest/index.html
- Team Knowledge Q&A (App, Knowledge): A knowledge layer for a team: pages, search and answers with their source. Every page has an owner, a class and a link to where it came from. knowledge-qa/index.html
- Team Memory Agent (Agent, Knowledge): Captures every hour and consolidates by code. A week becomes record only after you approve it. team-memory-agent/index.html
- Vault MCP (MCP server, Knowledge): An MCP server for the backlog, daily logs and briefs of a notes vault. 13 tools, no model inside, nothing leaves the PC. vault-mcp/index.html

# Skills

- Toilet Paper skill (Documents): Drives the Toilet Paper compiler: the agent writes a short source file, renders the diagram or document and checks that nothing published is older than its source.
- Deck and document builder (Documents): Plans a deck, a presentation or a branded document with you, then writes the source that Toilet Paper compiles. A deck source becomes an editable .pptx on the company master and one HTML file with the same look; a Markdown source becomes a Word document. It also starts an app page. It asks the format, the brand and the classification first, and writes nothing before you approve the plan.
- Craft apps (Documents): Installs, updates and runs a set of local Office and design apps by command line and MCP, with no admin rights: decks, documents, sheets, PDF, images, vectors, video and audio.
- Report builder (Build): The delivery line for a Power BI report. The idea is a mockup first: the mockup writes the specification and the contract, and a set of gates checks the delivery. What runs today is the audit of the semantic model against a curation checklist (an automated pass, an assisted review, a score per category), and a record of the steps, gates and cost of a delivery.
- Design review (Review): Reviews an HTML page against a design system while the page runs in a browser, at 3 screen widths, with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility checks and a measurement of the brand tokens.
- QA reviewer (Review): An adversarial reviewer for a diff, a file or a decision. It runs the tests that exist, then breaks every new or changed test on purpose, line by line. A test that still passes is reported as a problem. That mutation step caught an empty test on the first free-model task.
- Project coach (Planning): A pocket guide for running projects, anchored in a five-phase project process and the principles of PMBOK 7, pragmatic and not bureaucratic. It prepares a person for the conversation with a human mentor and does not replace it.
- OKR cycle (Planning): Runs a whole OKR cycle for a team: drafts and pressure-tests the OKRs, groups them into pillars, assigns owners, balances workload, defines a 75, 100 and 125 achievement-scoring model with weights, and generates executive one-pagers (bilingual HTML to PDF) and an Excel scorecard from a single spec file.
- Shipper (Build): Documentation, commit and push for the last mile. It fixes the docs the change made false, commits only its own paths in a clone that several sessions share, writes a conventional commit and closes the backlog idea with a script. It never stages everything.
- Fabric app method (Build): A method to create, develop and publish an app on Microsoft Fabric Apps with its CLI, in TypeScript: prepare the machine once, create the project with the team's rules, develop with Claude or Copilot, connect it to the data, review and publish.
- Session handoff (Knowledge): An end-of-session handoff. It summarizes the session into the notes vault, updates the index and log and leaves a context block, so any later Claude instance can resume without the conversation history.
- Vault start (Knowledge): Starts a session on a notes vault: loads the operating manual, restores the last session's context, checks the inbox and asks for the day's focus.
- Video to vault (Knowledge): Brings a video from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram or Vimeo into the notes vault, with the provenance written by code and the analysis proposed in the session.
- Autodev runner (Build): Runs a small task on a free model inside an isolated worktree under strict limits, then checks the result by code. Claude plans and reviews with a mutation check, and a team lead step caps the work. It never pushes.
- CDMP exam coach (Learning): An adaptive exam coach for the CDMP data management certification. It makes fresh practice questions one at a time, explains all five options the way an exam forum would, and tracks performance per domain and per concept, with diagnostic reports.
- Web research (Knowledge): Web research with the source and the date, using the session's own search, with no API key and no extra cost. It answers in the chat and writes no file. A colleague's name or an internal fact never goes into the search.
- Product coach (Planning): A pocket guide for defining what to build, the counterpart of the project coach. It writes a feature spec from a problem, updates a Now, Next, Later roadmap, turns research and feedback into themes and opportunities, and runs brainstorming that diverges and then converges.
- Portfolio project copilot (Planning): A copilot for project managers who work in a project portfolio tool. Its commands cover the charter, the work breakdown, the sprint and the status report, and it needs write access to a notes vault.
- App test personas (Review): Runs a round of tests on a desktop app with 4 test personas, 2 who know the app and 2 beginners. Each persona uses the real app in the built-in browser and writes test cases that the app's own test mode shows.
